title: Moses Recalls the Wilderness Years
summary: On the plains of Moab in the fortieth year Moses begins his address by recalling the departure from Horeb, the appointment of judges, and Israel's refusal to enter the land after the spies' report. He recounts the years in the wilderness, the defeat of Sihon and Og, and the land given to the eastern tribes. Moses says God was angry with him and would not let him cross; after he pleads, he is told to commission Joshua and view the land from Pisgah.

title: Call to Obey the Law
summary: Moses urges Israel to keep the statutes so that other nations will call them a wise and understanding people, and warns them not to add to the commands or make images, since at Horeb they heard a voice but saw no form. He foretells scattering if they turn to idols, followed by return if they seek the LORD with all their heart. He asks whether any other people has heard God speak from fire, and sets apart three cities of refuge east of the Jordan.

title: The Ten Commandments and the Shema
summary: Moses restates the Ten Commandments given at Horeb, recalling that the people feared the fire and asked him to speak for God. He then gives the central command, 'Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD', to love him with all heart, soul and might. These words are to be taught to children, talked of at home and on the road, bound on the hand and written on doorposts, and remembered when Israel is prosperous in the land.

title: Driving Out the Nations
summary: Israel is told to destroy the seven nations of Canaan, make no treaties or marriages with them, and expect blessing and fruitfulness in return. Moses recalls the testing in the wilderness and the manna, and warns that after prosperity Israel must not say its own power or righteousness won the land, since it is a stiff-necked people. He recounts the golden calf, the broken tablets, and his forty days of prayer for Israel and for Aaron.

title: The Second Tablets and the Choice
summary: Moses recalls God's second set of tablets, the ark of acacia wood, and the separation of the Levites. He asks what the LORD requires: fear, walking in his ways, love and service with all the heart. He reminds Israel what God did in Egypt and the wilderness and contrasts the land they will enter, watered by rain from heaven, with Egypt. He sets before them a blessing for obedience and a curse for disobedience, to be declared on Gerizim and Ebal.

title: Laws for Life in the Land
summary: Moses gives the laws for life in the land: worship at the one place God chooses, clean and unclean foods, tithes, release of debts and slaves in the seventh year, the three yearly feasts, judges and the king, Levites and prophets, cities of refuge, rules for war, and laws on family, property, justice and kindness to the poor. He ends with the offering of firstfruits and a declaration of the tithe, and Israel is told that it has declared the LORD to be its God.

title: Blessings and Curses of the Covenant
summary: Moses and the elders tell Israel to set up large stones plastered with lime at Mount Ebal and write the law on them, and to build an altar. Six tribes are to stand on Gerizim for the blessings and six on Ebal for the curses, with the Levites reciting curses to which the people answer Amen. Chapter 28 spells out blessings for obedience, then a far longer list of curses for disobedience, ending in siege, exile and a return to Egypt.

title: Renewal of the Covenant in Moab
summary: In the land of Moab, Moses renews the covenant with all Israel, including children and strangers, and warns that anyone who turns to other gods will bring the curses. He foretells exile and the nations' wonder at the ruined land, then restoration if the people return with all their heart. He says the commandment is not too hard or far away but near, and sets before them life and death, blessing and cursing, urging them to choose life.

title: Joshua Commissioned and the Song of Moses
summary: Moses, now 120, says he can no longer lead, encourages Joshua, and gives the written law to the priests to be read to all Israel every seventh year. God predicts Israel's rebellion, so Moses writes a song to be a witness against them that recalls God as a faithful Rock and Israel's unfaithfulness. God then tells Moses to climb Mount Nebo, see the land, and die there, because of what happened at Meribah.

title: Moses Blesses the Tribes and Dies
summary: Moses blesses each tribe in turn, beginning with the LORD coming from Sinai, and closes by calling Israel happy and saved by the LORD. He then climbs Mount Nebo, where the LORD shows him the land from Gilead to the south, and he dies there at 120 'according to the word of the LORD'. No one knows his grave. Israel mourns thirty days, Joshua takes up leadership, and the book says no prophet since has been like Moses.
